dedupe_keys.name: beeam building electrical efficiency analysis model modelica library

description: BEEAM, the Building Electrical Efficiency Analysis Model, is a Modelica library that simulates the efficiency of building electrical distribution systems using harmonic power flow. It was developed by Stephen Frank and colleagues at the National Renewable Energy Laboratory with Colorado State University, funded by the US Department of Energy Building Technologies Office, and registered on DOE CODE as SWR-20-107 in 2020. The motivation is the growing share of building loads that use direct current internally: the library compares three-phase AC, single-phase AC, unipolar DC, bipolar DC and hybrid networks under balanced and unbalanced loads, models power electronic converter losses, gives granular loss estimates across the system and handles part-load efficiency. BEEAM can be packaged as a Functional Mock-up Unit for co-simulation with other tools such as EnergyPlus. Coverage: generic building electrical systems, not tied to a place. Access: the DOE CODE record; the metadata read gives no repository address or licence, so both are to be confirmed. Caveats: this is an efficiency model of normal operation, not a fault or outage model. Simulation uses are comparing AC and DC building distribution designs and feeding building electrical losses into co-simulation with thermal and grid models. Related records: the EnergyPlus and Modelica Buildings Library records.
